jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Manager in the Luxury Sector
Whether in prestige hospitality, haute couture, or jewelry , the Manager in the Luxury Sector is an ambassador of excellence . Their role is to satisfy a demanding, high-end clientele by ensuring that every service is flawless and in line with the brand image they represent.
Responsibilities
The luxury sector is divided into two categories:
- Material Luxury (fashion, jewelry, leather goods, etc.)
- Experiential Luxury (tourism, hospitality, gastronomy), which represents 64% of the global market.
In this rapidly growing sector, the specialized Luxury Manager fulfills various missions:
- Maintain Brand Reputation: Define and implement a commercial policy consistent with the brand's image, recruit and supervise rare talents, and attract new clients.
- Cultivate Loyalty in High-End Clientele: Create a privileged relationship with the most important clients, devise personalized gestures, and guarantee a unique experience.
- Promote the Brand's History and Identity: Transmit the values, tell the story, and highlight the brand's distinguishing assets.
- Participate in the Communication Plan: Collaborate with marketing, suggest improvements, and adapt offerings to the evolving luxury market.
Did You Know?
The luxury industry is prosperous: in 2021, the global high-end luxury market represented nearly 283 billion euros (source: Les Échos).
Required Skills and Qualities
Technical Skills
- Cultural Knowledge: Understanding the customs, conventions, and expectations of an international clientele.
- Market Research Methods: Analyzing trends and purchasing behaviors to define an appropriate strategy.
- Pricing Management Techniques: Mastery of yield management (flexible pricing), particularly in hospitality.
- Luxury Codes: Adherence to the aesthetic, protocol, and behavioral standards specific to the sector.
- Foreign Languages: Fluent English is essential; Chinese or Russian are highly valued.
- Human Resources Management: Supervising and motivating teams (department heads, reception, sales, etc.).
Personal Qualities (Soft Skills)
- Rigor and attention to detail.
- Aesthetic sense and refinement.
- Adaptability and creativity.
- Excellent presentation and relational ease (interpersonal skills).
- Acute sense of service and prestige.
Education and Qualifications
To meet the sector's expectations, recruiters prioritize specialized training:
- Bachelor & MBA in Hotel Management, Business, or Luxury Management.
- Specialized MBAs (e.g., MBA in International Hospitality ) effectively prepare candidates for management positions in luxury by developing expertise in management, marketing, and high-end service.
Working Conditions
- Prestigious but highly demanding environment.
- Extended hours, often evenings or weekends.
- High international mobility depending on the position and the brand/house.
Salary
Compensation varies according to the sector, country, and level of responsibility:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Between €3,100 and €4,100 gross/month.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Between €5,000 and €8,000 gross/month, excluding bonuses and profit-sharing linked to revenue.
Career Progression
A manager specializing in luxury can progress toward:
- General management positions in hospitality, fashion, or jewelry.
- Managing multiple establishments or boutiques.
- Strategic roles (Brand Manager, Marketing Director, Commercial Director).
With experience, they can also move into luxury strategy consulting or entrepreneurship .
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Profili di lavoro
Manager nel settore del lusso
Che si tratti di ospitalità di prestigio, alta moda, o gioielli , il Manager nel settore del lusso è un ambasciatore di eccellenza . Il loro ruolo è quello di soddisfare una clientela esigente e di fascia alta garantendo che ogni servizio sia impeccabile e in linea con l'immagine di marca che rappresentano.
responsabilità
Il settore del lusso è diviso in due categorie:
- Materiale Lusso (fashion, gioielli, pelletteria, ecc.)
- Lusso esperienziale (turismo, ospitalità, gastronomia), che rappresenta il 64% del mercato globale.
In questo settore in rapida crescita, il Luxury Manager specializzato svolge diverse missioni:
- Mantenere Brand Reputation: Definire e implementare una politica commerciale coerente con l'immagine del marchio, reclutare e supervisionare i talenti rari e attirare nuovi clienti.
- Coltivare la Loyalty in High-End Clientele: creare un rapporto privilegiato con i clienti più importanti, ideare gesti personalizzati e garantire un'esperienza unica.
- Promuovere la storia e l'identità del marchio: Trasmettere i valori, raccontare la storia e mettere in evidenza i beni distintivi del marchio.
- Partecipa al Piano di Comunicazione: Collabora con il marketing, suggerisci miglioramenti e adatta le offerte al mercato del lusso in evoluzione.
Lo sapevi?
L'industria del lusso è prospera: nel 2021, il mercato globale di lusso di fascia alta rappresentava quasi 283 miliardi di euro (fonte: Les Échos).
Competenze e competenze richieste
Competenze tecniche
- Conoscenza culturale: comprensione delle usanze, convenzioni e aspettative di una clientela internazionale.
- Metodi di ricerca di mercato: analizzare tendenze e comportamenti di acquisto per definire una strategia appropriata.
- Tecniche di gestione dei prezzi: Mastery of yield management (prezzo flessibile), in particolare nell'ospitalità.
- Codici di Lusso: Aderenza agli standard estetici, protocolli e comportamentali specifici per il settore.
- Lingue straniere: L'inglese fluente è essenziale; il cinese o il russo sono molto apprezzati.
- Gestione delle risorse umane: supervisionare e motivare i team ( teste di di dipartimento, reception, vendita, ecc.).
QualitÃ Personali (Soft Skills)
- Rigor e attenzione ai dettagli.
- Senso estetico e raffinatezza.
- Adattabilità e creatività.
- Ottima presentazione e facilità relazionale (abilità interpersonali).
- Acuto senso di servizio e prestigio.
Istruzione e qualificazione
Per soddisfare le aspettative del settore, i reclutatori privilegiano la formazione specializzata:
- Bachelor & MBA in gestione alberghiera, business o gestione di lusso.
- Specializzato MBAs (ad esempio, MBA in International Hospitality) prepara efficacemente i candidati per le posizioni di gestione nel lusso sviluppando competenze in gestione, marketing e servizio di fascia alta.
Condizioni di lavoro
- Ambiente prestigioso ma altamente esigente.
- Ore prolungate, spesso serate o fine settimana.
- Alta mobilità internazionale a seconda della posizione e del marchio/casa.
Salari
La compensazione varia a seconda del settore, del paese e del livello di responsabilità:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Tra €3,100 e €4,100 lordo/mese.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Tra i 5.000 e i 8.000 euro lordi/mese, esclusi i bonus e la condivisione dei profitti legati alle entrate.
Progressione di carriera
Un manager specializzato nel lusso può progredire verso:
- posizioni di gestione generale in ospitalità, moda, o gioielli.
- Gestione di più stabilimenti o boutique.
- ruoli strategici (Brand Manager, Direttore Marketing, Direttore Commerciale).
Con esperienza, possono anche muoversi in consulenza di strategia di lusso o imprenditorialità .
Storie di successo dei laureati Vatel
In Francia e a livello internazionale, i 50.000 alunni di Vatel costruiscono ogni giorno carriere esemplari, innovative ed emozionanti. Lavorano in diversi settori come l'ospitalità di lusso, ristoranti gourmet, gestione eventi, marketing alberghiero, gestione del lusso, enologia, crociere, turismo internazionale, e l'industria del vino e dello spirito.

Job Profiles
Manager in the Luxury Sector
Whether in prestige hospitality, haute couture, or jewelry , the Manager in the Luxury Sector is an ambassador of excellence . Their role is to satisfy a demanding, high-end clientele by ensuring that every service is flawless and in line with the brand image they represent.
Responsibilities
The luxury sector is divided into two categories:
- Material Luxury (fashion, jewelry, leather goods, etc.)
- Experiential Luxury (tourism, hospitality, gastronomy), which represents 64% of the global market.
In this rapidly growing sector, the specialized Luxury Manager fulfills various missions:
- Maintain Brand Reputation: Define and implement a commercial policy consistent with the brand's image, recruit and supervise rare talents, and attract new clients.
- Cultivate Loyalty in High-End Clientele: Create a privileged relationship with the most important clients, devise personalized gestures, and guarantee a unique experience.
- Promote the Brand's History and Identity: Transmit the values, tell the story, and highlight the brand's distinguishing assets.
- Participate in the Communication Plan: Collaborate with marketing, suggest improvements, and adapt offerings to the evolving luxury market.
Did You Know?
The luxury industry is prosperous: in 2021, the global high-end luxury market represented nearly 283 billion euros (source: Les Échos).
Required Skills and Qualities
Technical Skills
- Cultural Knowledge: Understanding the customs, conventions, and expectations of an international clientele.
- Market Research Methods: Analyzing trends and purchasing behaviors to define an appropriate strategy.
- Pricing Management Techniques: Mastery of yield management (flexible pricing), particularly in hospitality.
- Luxury Codes: Adherence to the aesthetic, protocol, and behavioral standards specific to the sector.
- Foreign Languages: Fluent English is essential; Chinese or Russian are highly valued.
- Human Resources Management: Supervising and motivating teams (department heads, reception, sales, etc.).
Personal Qualities (Soft Skills)
- Rigor and attention to detail.
- Aesthetic sense and refinement.
- Adaptability and creativity.
- Excellent presentation and relational ease (interpersonal skills).
- Acute sense of service and prestige.
Education and Qualifications
To meet the sector's expectations, recruiters prioritize specialized training:
- Bachelor & MBA in Hotel Management, Business, or Luxury Management.
- Specialized MBAs (e.g., MBA in International Hospitality ) effectively prepare candidates for management positions in luxury by developing expertise in management, marketing, and high-end service.
Working Conditions
- Prestigious but highly demanding environment.
- Extended hours, often evenings or weekends.
- High international mobility depending on the position and the brand/house.
Salary
Compensation varies according to the sector, country, and level of responsibility:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Between €3,100 and €4,100 gross/month.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Between €5,000 and €8,000 gross/month, excluding bonuses and profit-sharing linked to revenue.
Career Progression
A manager specializing in luxury can progress toward:
- General management positions in hospitality, fashion, or jewelry.
- Managing multiple establishments or boutiques.
- Strategic roles (Brand Manager, Marketing Director, Commercial Director).
With experience, they can also move into luxury strategy consulting or entrepreneurship .

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Jobprofile
Manager im Luxussektor
Ob in der renommierten Gastfreundschaft, Haute Couture oder Schmuck, der Manager im Luxussektor ist ein Botschafter der Exzellenz. Ihre Aufgabe ist es, eine anspruchsvolle, hochwertige Kundschaft zu befriedigen, indem sie sicherstellt, dass jeder Service makellos ist und dem Markenimage entspricht, das sie repräsentieren.
Zuständigkeiten
Der Luxussektor ist in zwei Kategorien unterteilt:
- Material Luxus (Mode, Schmuck, Lederwaren, etc.)
- Experiential Luxury (Tourismus, Gastfreundschaft, Gastronomie), die 64% des globalen Marktes ausmacht.
In diesem schnell wachsenden Sektor erfüllt der spezialisierte Luxury Manager verschiedene Aufgaben:
- Markenreputation bewahren: Definieren und implementieren Sie eine Geschäftspolitik, die mit dem Image der Marke übereinstimmt, rekrutieren und beaufsichtigen Sie seltene Talente und gewinnen Sie neue Kunden.
- Pflegen Sie Loyalität in High-End-Kunden: Schaffen Sie eine privilegierte Beziehung zu den wichtigsten Kunden, entwickeln Sie personalisierte Gesten und garantieren Sie ein einzigartiges Erlebnis.
- Die Geschichte und Identität der Marke fördern: Übertragen Sie die Werte, erzählen Sie die Geschichte und heben Sie die charakteristischen Vermögenswerte der Marke hervor.
- Nehmen Sie am Kommunikationsplan teil: Arbeiten Sie mit dem Marketing zusammen, schlagen Sie Verbesserungen vor und passen Sie die Angebote an den sich entwickelnden Luxusmarkt an.
Wussten Sie das?
Die Luxusbranche ist florierend: Im Jahr 2021 machte der globale High-End-Luxusmarkt fast 283 Milliarden Euro aus (Quelle: Les Échos).
Erforderliche Fähigkeiten und Qualitäten
Technische Fähigkeiten
- Kulturelles Wissen: Die Bräuche, Konventionen und Erwartungen einer internationalen Kundschaft verstehen.
- Marktforschungsmethoden: Analyse von Trends und Kaufverhalten, um eine angemessene Strategie zu definieren.
- Pricing Management Techniken: Beherrschung des Yield Managements (flexible Pricing), insbesondere im Gastgewerbe.
- Luxus-Codes: Einhaltung der für die Branche spezifischen ästhetischen, Protokoll- und Verhaltensstandards.
- Fremdsprachen: fließendes Englisch ist unerlässlich; Chinesisch oder Russisch werden hoch geschätzt.
- Personalmanagement: Betreuung und Motivation von Teams (Abteilungsleiter, Rezeption, Verkauf, etc.).
Persönliche Qualitäten (Soft Skills)
- Strenge und Liebe zum Detail.
- Ästhetischer Sinn und Raffinesse.
- Anpassungsfähigkeit und Kreativität.
- Hervorragende Präsentation und relationale Leichtigkeit (zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten).
- Akuter Sinn für Service und Prestige.
Ausbildung und Qualifikationen
Um die Erwartungen der Branche zu erfüllen, priorisieren Personalvermittler spezialisierte Schulungen:
- Bachelor & MBA in Hotelmanagement, Business oder Luxusmanagement.
- Spezialisierte MBAs (z. B. MBA in International Hospitality) bereiten Kandidaten effektiv auf Managementpositionen im Luxus vor, indem sie Fachwissen in Management, Marketing und High-End-Service entwickeln.
Arbeitsbedingungen
- Ansehendes, aber sehr anspruchsvolles Umfeld.
- Verlängerte Stunden, oft Abende oder Wochenenden.
- Hohe internationale Mobilität je nach Position und Marke/Haus.
Gehalt
Die Vergütung variiert je nach Sektor, Land und Verantwortungsgrad:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Zwischen 3.100 € und 4.100 € brutto/Monat.
- Luxushoteldirektor: zwischen 5.000 € und 8.000 € brutto/Monat, ohne Boni und Gewinnbeteiligung in Verbindung mit dem Umsatz.
Karrierefortschritt
Ein auf Luxus spezialisierter Manager kann Fortschritte machen in Richtung:
- General Management-Positionen in der Gastfreundschaft, Mode oder Schmuck.
- Verwaltung mehrerer Einrichtungen oder Boutiquen.
- Strategische Rollen (Brand Manager, Marketing Director, Commercial Director).
Mit Erfahrung können sie auch in Luxusstrategieberatung oder Unternehmertum einsteigen.
Erfolgsgeschichten von Vatel Absolventen
In Frankreich und international bauen die 50.000 Vatel Alumni jeden Tag vorbildliche, innovative und spannende Karrieren auf. Sie arbeiten in verschiedenen Bereichen wie Luxushotellerie, Gourmetrestaurants, Eventmanagement, Hotelmarketing, Luxusmanagement, Önologie, Kreuzfahrten, internationalem Tourismus und der Wein- und Spirituosenindustrie.

Profils d'emploi
Gestionnaire dans le secteur du luxe
Que ce soit dans l'hospitalité de prestige, la haute couture, ou les bijoux, le directeur dans le secteur du luxe est un ambassadeur d'excellence. Leur rôle est de satisfaire une clientèle exigeante et haut de gamme en s'assurant que chaque service est impeccable et conforme à l'image de marque qu'ils représentent.
Responsabilités
Le secteur du luxe est divisé en deux catégories :
- Matériel Luxe (fashion, bijoux, maroquinerie, etc.)
- Le luxe expérientiel (tourisme, hospitalité, gastronomie), qui représente 64% du marché mondial.
Dans ce secteur en croissance rapide, le gestionnaire de luxe spécialisé remplit diverses missions :
- Maintenir la réputation de la marque : Définir et mettre en oeuvre une politique commerciale conforme à l'image de marque, recruter et superviser des talents rares et attirer de nouveaux clients.
- Cultiver la loyauté dans le clientèle haut de gamme : créer une relation privilégiée avec les clients les plus importants, concevoir des gestes personnalisés et garantir une expérience unique.
- Promouvoir l'histoire et l'identité de la marque : Transmettre les valeurs, raconter l'histoire et souligner les atouts distinctifs de la marque.
- Participer au plan de communication : Collaborer avec le marketing, suggérer des améliorations et adapter les offres au marché du luxe en évolution.
Le saviez - vous?
L'industrie du luxe est prospère : en 2021, le marché mondial du luxe haut de gamme représentait près de 283 milliards d'euros (source : Les Échos).
Compétences et qualités requises
Compétences techniques
- Connaissances culturelles : Comprendre les coutumes, les conventions et les attentes d'une clientèle internationale.
- Méthodes d'études de marché : Analyser les tendances et les comportements d'achat pour définir une stratégie appropriée.
- Techniques de gestion des prix : Maîtrise de la gestion des rendements (prix flexibles), particulièrement en hospitalité.
- Codes de luxe : Respect des normes esthétiques, protocolaires et comportementales propres au secteur.
- Langues étrangères : L'anglais fluide est essentiel ; le chinois ou le russe sont très appréciés.
- Gestion des ressources humaines : Superviser et motiver les équipes (chefs de département, réception, ventes, etc.).
Qualités personnelles (compétences souples)
- Rigeur et attention au détail.
- Sens esthétique et raffinement.
- Adaptabilité et créativité.
- Excellente présentation et facilité relationnelle (compétences interpersonnelles).
- Sens aigu du service et du prestige.
Éducation et qualifications
Pour répondre aux attentes du secteur, les recruteurs privilégient la formation spécialisée :
- Bachelor & MBA en gestion d'hôtel, d'affaires ou de luxe.
- Les MBA spécialisés (p. ex. MBA in International Hospitality ) préparent efficacement les candidats à des postes de gestion dans le luxe en développant une expertise en gestion, en marketing et en service haut de gamme.
Conditions de travail
- Un environnement prestigieux mais très exigeant.
- Heures prolongées, souvent le soir ou le week-end.
- Mobilité internationale élevée selon la position et la marque/maison.
Salaire
La rémunération varie selon le secteur, le pays et le niveau de responsabilité:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Entre 3 100 € et 4 100 € brut/mois.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Entre 5 000 et 8 000 € brut/mois, hors bonus et participation au bénéfice liée au chiffre d'affaires.
Évolution de carrière
Un gestionnaire spécialisé dans le luxe peut progresser vers :
- Postes de gestion générale en hospitalité, mode ou bijoux.
- Gestion de plusieurs établissements ou boutiques.
- Rôles stratégiques (Gestionnaire de marque, Directeur du marketing, Directeur du commerce).
Avec l'expérience, ils peuvent également passer à la stratégie de luxe conseil ou l'entrepreneuriat.
Réussites des diplômés de Vatel
En France et à l'international, les 50 000 anciens élèves du Vatel construisent chaque jour des carrières exemplaires, innovantes et passionnantes. Ils travaillent dans divers secteurs comme l'hospitalité de luxe, les restaurants gastronomiques, la gestion d'événements, le marketing hôtelier, la gestion de luxe, l'œnologie, les croisières, le tourisme international et l'industrie du vin et des spiritueux.

jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Tourism and Hospitality Client Manager – Banking and Finance
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank.
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank. He/she supports hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, and other tourism businesses with account management, project financing, and cash flow optimization.
He/she acts as a dedicated point of contact, combining financial expertise with an in-depth understanding of the tourism industry.
Key 
• Responsibilities
The role of a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality industry is to develop and retain a portfolio of professional clients within the tourism industry. Their main responsibilities include:
Client account management and monitoring: Following up on financial transactions, analyzing client needs and profitability, and providing personalized advice to optimize cash flow and investments.
Business development: Prospecting for new clients and creating financial solutions tailored to the industry's specific needs, such as loans, leasing, insurance, and financing for hotel or tourism projects.
Project support: Advising on financing solutions for the construction, renovation, or expansion of hotels and tourism facilities.
Client relations and retention : Maintaining regular contact with clients, monitoring their performance, anticipating their needs, and proposing custom solutions.
Required Skills
To succeed in this position, several skills are essential:
Financial and accounting skills: Expertise in financial analysis, banking products, and financing solutions.
Knowledge of the tourism/hospitality sector: Understanding the economic challenges, operational specifics, and business cycles of the industry.
Communication and client relations: The ability to negotiate, advise, and retain clients.
Organization and rigor: The capacity to manage multiple files simultaneously and adhere to banking procedures.
Proficiency in English and other foreign languages: Essential for dealing with international clients.
Education
A bachelor's or master's degree is generally required, with a specialization in banking, finance, management, or business. A background in hospitality and tourism ( MBA or Bachelor at Vatel) supplemented by financial training can also lead to this role. Experience in the tourism or hotel sector is highly valued.
Salary
The average salary for a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality ranges from €30,000 to €45,000 gross per year at the beginning of their career. With experience and depending on the size of the bank or the complexity of their portfolio, it can reach €60,000 or more.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Client Manager can advance to:
Senior Professional Client Portfolio Manager
Bank Branch Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality
Corporate or Professional Market Relations Manager
Hotel and Tourism Financing Consultant

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Profili di lavoro
Gestione clienti del turismo e dell'ospitalità – Banca e finanza
Client Manager specializzato nel settore del turismo e dell'ospitalità è un professionista della gestione delle relazioni che lavora all'interno di una banca.
Client Manager specializzato nel settore del turismo e dell'ospitalità è un professionista della gestione delle relazioni che lavora all'interno di una banca. Supporta hotel, agenzie di viaggio, tour operator e altre aziende turistiche con gestione account, finanziamento di progetti e ottimizzazione dei flussi di cassa.
Agisce come punto di contatto dedicato, combinando competenze finanziarie con una comprensione approfondita dell'industria del turismo.
Chiave
• responsabilità
Il ruolo di Customer Manager specializzato nel settore del turismo e dell'ospitalità è quello di sviluppare e conservare un portafoglio di clienti professionali all'interno del settore del turismo. Le loro principali responsabilità includono:
Gestione e monitoraggio dell'account cliente: In seguito alle transazioni finanziarie, analizzando le esigenze del cliente e la redditività, e fornendo consigli personalizzati per ottimizzare il flusso di cassa e gli investimenti.
Sviluppo aziendale: Prospezione per nuovi clienti e creazione di soluzioni finanziarie su misura per le esigenze specifiche del settore, come prestiti, leasing, assicurazioni e finanziamenti per progetti alberghieri o turistici.
Supporto del progetto: consulenza sul finanziamento di soluzioni per la costruzione, la ristrutturazione o l'espansione di hotel e strutture turistiche.
Rapporti e fidelizzazione dei clienti: Mantenere contatti regolari con i clienti, monitorare le loro prestazioni, anticipare le loro esigenze e proporre soluzioni personalizzate.
Competenze richieste
Per avere successo in questa posizione, diverse competenze sono essenziali:
Competenze finanziarie e contabili: competenza nell'analisi finanziaria, nei prodotti bancari e nelle soluzioni di finanziamento.
Conoscenza del settore turistico/ospitalitÃ: comprensione delle sfide economiche, delle specifiche operative e dei cicli aziendali dell'industria.
Comunicazione e relazioni con i clienti: la capacità di negoziare, consigliare e mantenere i clienti.
Organizzazione e rigore: La capacità di gestire più file contemporaneamente e aderire alle procedure bancarie.
La competenza in inglese e in altre lingue straniere: essenziale per trattare con i clienti internazionali.
Istruzione
Un diploma di laurea o master è generalmente richiesto, con una specializzazione in banca, finanza, gestione o affari. Un background in ospitalità e turismo (MBA o Bachelor a Vatel) completato da formazione finanziaria può anche portare a questo ruolo. L'esperienza nel settore turistico o alberghiero è molto apprezzata.
Salari
Lo stipendio medio per un Customer Manager specializzato nel turismo e nell'ospitalità varia da 30.000 a 45.000 euro all'anno all'inizio della loro carriera. Con esperienza e a seconda delle dimensioni della banca o della complessità del loro portafoglio, può raggiungere €60.000 o più.
Progressione di carriera
Dopo diversi anni di esperienza, un Client Manager può avanzare a:
Responsabile portafoglio clienti professionali senior
Bank Branch Manager specializzata nel turismo e nell'ospitalità
Corporate o Professional Market Relations Manager

In Francia e a livello internazionale, i 50.000 alunni di Vatel costruiscono ogni giorno carriere esemplari, innovative ed emozionanti. Lavorano in diversi settori come l'ospitalità di lusso, ristoranti gourmet, gestione eventi, marketing alberghiero, gestione del lusso, enologia, crociere, turismo internazionale, e l'industria del vino e dello spirito.

Job Profiles
Tourism and Hospitality Client Manager – Banking and Finance
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank.
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank. He/she supports hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, and other tourism businesses with account management, project financing, and cash flow optimization.
He/she acts as a dedicated point of contact, combining financial expertise with an in-depth understanding of the tourism industry.
Key 
• Responsibilities
The role of a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality industry is to develop and retain a portfolio of professional clients within the tourism industry. Their main responsibilities include:
Client account management and monitoring: Following up on financial transactions, analyzing client needs and profitability, and providing personalized advice to optimize cash flow and investments.
Business development: Prospecting for new clients and creating financial solutions tailored to the industry's specific needs, such as loans, leasing, insurance, and financing for hotel or tourism projects.
Project support: Advising on financing solutions for the construction, renovation, or expansion of hotels and tourism facilities.
Client relations and retention : Maintaining regular contact with clients, monitoring their performance, anticipating their needs, and proposing custom solutions.
Required Skills
To succeed in this position, several skills are essential:
Financial and accounting skills: Expertise in financial analysis, banking products, and financing solutions.
Knowledge of the tourism/hospitality sector: Understanding the economic challenges, operational specifics, and business cycles of the industry.
Communication and client relations: The ability to negotiate, advise, and retain clients.
Organization and rigor: The capacity to manage multiple files simultaneously and adhere to banking procedures.
Proficiency in English and other foreign languages: Essential for dealing with international clients.
Education
A bachelor's or master's degree is generally required, with a specialization in banking, finance, management, or business. A background in hospitality and tourism ( MBA or Bachelor at Vatel) supplemented by financial training can also lead to this role. Experience in the tourism or hotel sector is highly valued.
Salary
The average salary for a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality ranges from €30,000 to €45,000 gross per year at the beginning of their career. With experience and depending on the size of the bank or the complexity of their portfolio, it can reach €60,000 or more.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Client Manager can advance to:
Senior Professional Client Portfolio Manager
Bank Branch Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality
Corporate or Professional Market Relations Manager
Hotel and Tourism Financing Consultant
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Jobprofile
Tourismus und Hospitality Client Manager - Banking und Finanzen
Der auf die Tourismus- und Hotelleriebranche spezialisierte Client Manager ist ein Relationship Management-Experte, der in einer Bank arbeitet.
Der auf die Tourismus- und Hotelleriebranche spezialisierte Client Manager ist ein Relationship Management-Experte, der in einer Bank arbeitet. Er unterstützt Hotels, Reisebüros, Reiseveranstalter und andere Tourismusunternehmen bei der Kontoverwaltung, Projektfinanzierung und Cashflow-Optimierung.
Er / sie fungiert als engagierter Ansprechpartner, der Finanzexpertise mit einem tiefen Verständnis der Tourismusbranche kombiniert.
Schlüssel
• Zuständigkeiten
Die Rolle eines Kundenmanagers, der sich auf die Tourismus- und Hotelleriebranche spezialisiert hat, besteht darin, ein Portfolio professioneller Kunden in der Tourismusbranche zu entwickeln und zu behalten. Zu ihren Hauptaufgaben gehören:
Kundenkontoverwaltung und -überwachung: Nachverfolgung von Finanztransaktionen, Analyse der Kundenbedürfnisse und Rentabilität sowie personalisierte Beratung zur Optimierung des Cashflows und der Investitionen.
Geschäftsentwicklung: Suche nach neuen Kunden und Schaffung von Finanzlösungen, die auf die spezifischen Bedürfnisse der Branche zugeschnitten sind, wie Darlehen, Leasing, Versicherung und Finanzierung von Hotel- oder Tourismusprojekten.
Projektunterstützung: Beratung bei Finanzierungslösungen für den Bau, die Renovierung oder den Ausbau von Hotels und touristischen Einrichtungen.
Kundenbeziehungen und -bindung: Pflegen Sie regelmäßigen Kontakt mit Kunden, überwachen Sie ihre Leistung, antizipieren Sie ihre Bedürfnisse und schlagen Sie kundenspezifische Lösungen vor.
Erforderliche Fähigkeiten
Um in dieser Position erfolgreich zu sein, sind mehrere Fähigkeiten unerlässlich:
Finanz- und Buchhaltungskompetenz: Expertise in Finanzanalysen, Bankprodukten und Finanzierungslösungen.
Kenntnisse des Tourismus- / Gastfreundschaftssektors: Verständnis der wirtschaftlichen Herausforderungen, operativen Besonderheiten und Geschäftszyklen der Branche.
Kommunikation und Kundenbeziehungen: Die Fähigkeit, Kunden zu verhandeln, zu beraten und zu halten.
Organisation und Strenge: Die Fähigkeit, mehrere Dateien gleichzeitig zu verwalten und Bankverfahren einzuhalten.
Kenntnisse in Englisch und anderen Fremdsprachen: Unverzichtbar für den Umgang mit internationalen Kunden.
Bildung
Ein Bachelor- oder Master-Abschluss ist in der Regel erforderlich, mit einer Spezialisierung in Banking, Finanzen, Management oder Business. Ein Hintergrund in Gastfreundschaft und Tourismus (MBA oder Bachelor bei Vatel) ergänzt durch finanzielle Ausbildung kann auch zu dieser Rolle führen. Erfahrung im Tourismus- oder Hotelsektor wird sehr geschätzt.
Gehalt
Das durchschnittliche Gehalt eines Kundenmanagers, der sich auf Tourismus und Gastgewerbe spezialisiert hat, liegt zu Beginn seiner Karriere zwischen 30.000 € und 45.000 € brutto pro Jahr. Mit Erfahrung und abhängig von der Größe der Bank oder der Komplexität ihres Portfolios kann es 60.000 € oder mehr erreichen.
Karrierefortschritt
Nach mehreren Jahren Erfahrung kann ein Kundenmanager Folgendes erreichen:
Senior Professional Client Portfolio Manager
Bank Branch Manager, spezialisiert auf Tourismus und Gastfreundschaft
Corporate oder Professional Market Relations Manager
Hotel- und Tourismusfinanzierungsberater
Erfolgsgeschichten von Vatel Absolventen
In Frankreich und international bauen die 50.000 Vatel Alumni jeden Tag vorbildliche, innovative und spannende Karrieren auf. Sie arbeiten in verschiedenen Bereichen wie Luxushotellerie, Gourmetrestaurants, Eventmanagement, Hotelmarketing, Luxusmanagement, Önologie, Kreuzfahrten, internationalem Tourismus und der Wein- und Spirituosenindustrie.

Profils d'emploi
Directeur client du tourisme et de l'accueil – Services bancaires et finances
Client Manager spécialisé dans le tourisme et l'hôtellerie est un professionnel de la gestion des relations qui travaille au sein d'une banque.
Client Manager spécialisé dans le tourisme et l'hôtellerie est un professionnel de la gestion des relations qui travaille au sein d'une banque. Il soutient les hôtels, les agences de voyages, les voyagistes et d'autres entreprises touristiques avec la gestion de compte, le financement de projets et l'optimisation des flux de trésorerie.
Il agit comme un point de contact dédié, combinant expertise financière et compréhension approfondie de l'industrie du tourisme.
Clé
• Responsabilités
Le rôle d'un gestionnaire client spécialisé dans l'industrie du tourisme et de l'hôtellerie est de développer et de conserver un portefeuille de clients professionnels au sein de l'industrie du tourisme. Leurs principales responsabilités sont les suivantes :
Gestion et suivi des comptes clients : Suivi des transactions financières, analyse des besoins et de la rentabilité des clients et prestation de conseils personnalisés pour optimiser les flux de trésorerie et les investissements.
Développement des entreprises : Prospection de nouveaux clients et création de solutions financières adaptées aux besoins spécifiques de l'industrie, telles que prêts, leasing, assurance et financement de projets hôteliers ou touristiques.
Appui au projet: conseils sur les solutions de financement pour la construction, la rénovation ou l'expansion d'hôtels et d'installations touristiques.
Relations avec les clients et rétention : maintenir un contact régulier avec les clients, surveiller leurs performances, anticiper leurs besoins et proposer des solutions personnalisées.
Compétences requises
Pour réussir dans ce poste, plusieurs compétences sont essentielles :
Compétences financières et comptables : Expertise en analyse financière, produits bancaires et solutions de financement.
Connaissance du secteur du tourisme et de l'hospitalité : Comprendre les défis économiques, les spécificités opérationnelles et les cycles économiques de l'industrie.
Communication et relations avec les clients : Capacité de négocier, de conseiller et de retenir les clients.
Organisation et rigueur : Capacité de gérer plusieurs dossiers simultanément et de respecter les procédures bancaires.
Maîtrise de l'anglais et des autres langues étrangères : essentiel pour traiter avec des clients internationaux.
Éducation
Un baccalauréat ou une maîtrise est généralement requis, avec une spécialisation en banque, finance, gestion ou affaires. Une formation en hôtellerie et tourisme (MBA ou Bachelor at Vatel) complétée par une formation financière peut également mener à ce rôle. L'expérience dans le secteur du tourisme ou de l'hôtellerie est très appréciée.
Salaire
Le salaire moyen d'un Client Manager spécialisé dans le tourisme et l'accueil varie de 30 000 € à 45 000 € brut par an au début de leur carrière. Avec l'expérience et en fonction de la taille de la banque ou de la complexité de leur portefeuille, il peut atteindre 60 000 euros ou plus.
Évolution de carrière
Après plusieurs années d'expérience, un gestionnaire client peut avancer vers :
Gestionnaire de portefeuille professionnel principal
Directeur de la succursale bancaire spécialisée dans le tourisme et l'accueil
Gestionnaire des relations commerciales entre les entreprises et les professionnels
Consultant en financement de l'hôtellerie et du tourisme
Réussites des diplômés de Vatel
En France et à l'international, les 50 000 anciens élèves du Vatel construisent chaque jour des carrières exemplaires, innovantes et passionnantes. Ils travaillent dans divers secteurs comme l'hospitalité de luxe, les restaurants gastronomiques, la gestion d'événements, le marketing hôtelier, la gestion de luxe, l'œnologie, les croisières, le tourisme international et l'industrie du vin et des spiritueux.

jobs.title: Hotel Auditor
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Hotel Auditor
The Hotel Auditor is a professional specialized in evaluating the performance, compliance, and profitability of a hotel or tourist establishment. His/her role is to analyze management practices, service quality, regulatory compliance, and profitability in order to propose strategic recommendations . As a true expert in control and consulting, he/she assists hotels, resorts, and hotel chains in optimizing their operations and competitiveness.
Responsibilities
- Evaluate financial and operational management: Control budgets, costs, billing, and profit margins.
- Analyze compliance and service quality: Verify adherence to hygiene, safety, and quality standards (ISO, hotel labels, brand standards).
- Observe and audit processes: Analyze the work organization across various departments (accommodation, catering, front office, housekeeping, F&B).
- Measure client satisfaction: Through surveys, mystery audits, and monitoring online reviews.
- Formulate strategic recommendations: Suggest areas for improvement to optimize performance, reduce costs, or increase client satisfaction.
- Support management: Provide an external and objective perspective to guide strategic decisions.
Required Skills
- Solid knowledge of hotel management and financial analysis.
- Mastery of quality, safety, and hotel regulatory standards.
- Capacity for observation, analysis, and synthesis.
- Communication skills to present results and convince management.
- A sense of teaching (pedagogy) and guidance in change management.
- Good command of IT tools (reporting, ERP, hotel management software).
- Fluency in foreign languages (English in particular) is an asset for auditing international establishments.
Education to Become a Hotel Auditor
A degree level of Bac+3 to Bac+5 (Bachelor's to Master's equivalent) is generally required:
- Bachelor's in Hotel Management , Management, Audit, or Finance.
- MBA specialized in hospitality management or in audit and management control.
- Prior experience in the hotel industry (management, revenue management, management control, quality) is highly valued.
Specific certifications in quality auditing or internal control may complement the professional background.
Salary of a Hotel Auditor
- Entry-level: Between €2,800 and €3,500 gross per month.
- Confirmed Profile (Experienced): Between €3,500 and €5,000 gross per month.
- Senior or Independent: Up to €6,000 or more, depending on the size and reputation of the audited establishments.
Career Progression
After a few years, the Hotel Auditor can progress to roles such as:
- Quality Director in a hotel chain.
- Management Controller specializing in the hotel sector.
- Independent Consultant in the hotel and tourism industry.
- Hotel Director or Department Head (Accommodation, Catering, F&B) with reinforced expertise in operational steering.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Profili di lavoro
Hotel Auditor
L'Auditor Hotel è un professionista specializzato nella valutazione delle prestazioni, della conformità e della redditività di un hotel o di uno stabilimento turistico. Il suo ruolo è quello di analizzare le pratiche di gestione, la qualità del servizio, la conformità normativa e la redditività al fine di proporre raccomandazioni strategiche. Come vero esperto nel controllo e nella consulenza, assiste hotel, resort e catene alberghiere nell'ottimizzazione delle loro operazioni e della loro competitività.
responsabilità
- Valutare la gestione finanziaria e operativa: Bilanci di controllo, costi, fatturazione e margini di profitto.
- Analizza la conformità e la qualità del servizio: verifica l'aderenza agli standard di igiene, sicurezza e qualità (ISO, etichette alberghiere, standard di marca).
- Processi di osservazione e audit: Analizzare l'organizzazione di lavoro in vari dipartimenti (accomodazione, catering, front office, pulizia, F&B).
- Misurare la soddisfazione del cliente: attraverso sondaggi, verifiche misteriose e monitoraggio delle recensioni online.
- Formulare raccomandazioni strategiche: Suggerisci aree per il miglioramento per ottimizzare le prestazioni, ridurre i costi, o aumentare la soddisfazione del cliente.
- Gestione del supporto: fornire una prospettiva esterna e obiettiva per guidare le decisioni strategiche.
Competenze richieste
- Conoscenza solida della gestione alberghiera e dell'analisi finanziaria.
- Mastery di qualità, sicurezza e standard di regolazione alberghiera.
- Capacità di osservazione, analisi e sintesi.
- Capacità di comunicazione per presentare i risultati e convincere la gestione.
- Un senso di insegnamento (pedagogia) e guida nella gestione dei cambiamenti.
- Buon comando degli strumenti IT (reporting, ERP, software di gestione alberghiera).
- La fluidità nelle lingue straniere (in particolare l'inglese) è una risorsa per l'audit degli istituti internazionali.
Istruzione per Diventare un Hotel Auditor
Un livello di grado di Bac+3 a Bac+5 (Bachelor's to Master's equivalent) è generalmente richiesto:
- Laurea in gestione alberghiera, gestione, controllo o finanza.
- MBA specializzata nella gestione dell'ospitalità o nel controllo dell'audit e della gestione.
- La prima esperienza nel settore alberghiero (gestione, gestione dei ricavi, controllo della gestione, qualità) è altamente apprezzata.
Certificazioni specifiche nel controllo della qualità o del controllo interno possono integrare lo sfondo professionale.
Salario di un Hotel Auditor
- Livello di entrata: Tra 2.800 euro e 3.500 euro al mese.
- Profilo confermato (esperti): Tra 3,500 e 5.000 euro al mese.
- Senior o Independent: Fino a € 6.000 o più, a seconda delle dimensioni e della reputazione degli istituti controllati.
Progressione di carriera
Dopo alcuni anni, l'Auditor dell'Hotel può progredire in ruoli come:
- Direttore di qualità in una catena di hotel.
- Management Controller specializzato nel settore alberghiero.
- Consulente indipendente nel settore alberghiero e turistico.
- Hotel Director o Department Head (Accommodation, Catering, F&B) con competenze rafforzate nello sterzo operativo.
Storie di successo dei laureati Vatel
In Francia e a livello internazionale, i 50.000 alunni di Vatel costruiscono ogni giorno carriere esemplari, innovative ed emozionanti. Job Profiles
Hotel Auditor
The Hotel Auditor is a professional specialized in evaluating the performance, compliance, and profitability of a hotel or tourist establishment. His/her role is to analyze management practices, service quality, regulatory compliance, and profitability in order to propose strategic recommendations . As a true expert in control and consulting, he/she assists hotels, resorts, and hotel chains in optimizing their operations and competitiveness.
Responsibilities
- Evaluate financial and operational management: Control budgets, costs, billing, and profit margins.
- Analyze compliance and service quality: Verify adherence to hygiene, safety, and quality standards (ISO, hotel labels, brand standards).
- Observe and audit processes: Analyze the work organization across various departments (accommodation, catering, front office, housekeeping, F&B).
- Measure client satisfaction: Through surveys, mystery audits, and monitoring online reviews.
- Formulate strategic recommendations: Suggest areas for improvement to optimize performance, reduce costs, or increase client satisfaction.
- Support management: Provide an external and objective perspective to guide strategic decisions.
Required Skills
- Solid knowledge of hotel management and financial analysis.
- Mastery of quality, safety, and hotel regulatory standards.
- Capacity for observation, analysis, and synthesis.
- Communication skills to present results and convince management.
- A sense of teaching (pedagogy) and guidance in change management.
- Good command of IT tools (reporting, ERP, hotel management software).
- Fluency in foreign languages (English in particular) is an asset for auditing international establishments.
Education to Become a Hotel Auditor
A degree level of Bac+3 to Bac+5 (Bachelor's to Master's equivalent) is generally required:
- Bachelor's in Hotel Management , Management, Audit, or Finance.
- MBA specialized in hospitality management or in audit and management control.
- Prior experience in the hotel industry (management, revenue management, management control, quality) is highly valued.
Specific certifications in quality auditing or internal control may complement the professional background.
Salary of a Hotel Auditor
- Entry-level: Between €2,800 and €3,500 gross per month.
- Confirmed Profile (Experienced): Between €3,500 and €5,000 gross per month.
- Senior or Independent: Up to €6,000 or more, depending on the size and reputation of the audited establishments.
Career Progression
After a few years, the Hotel Auditor can progress to roles such as:
- Quality Director in a hotel chain.
- Management Controller specializing in the hotel sector.
- Independent Consultant in the hotel and tourism industry.
- Hotel Director or Department Head (Accommodation, Catering, F&B) with reinforced expertise in operational steering.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Jobprofile
Hotel Auditor
Der Hotel Auditor ist ein Fachmann, der sich auf die Bewertung der Leistung, Compliance und Rentabilität eines Hotels oder einer touristischen Einrichtung spezialisiert hat. Seine Aufgabe besteht darin, Managementpraktiken, Servicequalität, Einhaltung gesetzlicher Vorschriften und Rentabilität zu analysieren, um strategische Empfehlungen vorzuschlagen. Als echter Experte für Kontrolle und Beratung unterstützt er Hotels, Resorts und Hotelketten bei der Optimierung ihres Betriebs und ihrer Wettbewerbsfähigkeit.
Zuständigkeiten
- Bewerten Sie das Finanz- und Betriebsmanagement: Kontrollbudgets, Kosten, Abrechnung und Gewinnmargen.
- Compliance und Servicequalität analysieren: Überprüfen Sie die Einhaltung von Hygiene-, Sicherheits- und Qualitätsstandards (ISO, Hotellabels, Markenstandards).
- Beobachten und Auditprozesse: Analysieren Sie die Arbeitsorganisation in verschiedenen Abteilungen (Unterkunft, Catering, Front Office, Housekeeping, F&B).
- Messen Sie die Kundenzufriedenheit: Durch Umfragen, Mystery-Audits und die Überwachung von Online-Bewertungen.
- Formulieren Sie strategische Empfehlungen: Schlagen Sie Verbesserungsbereiche vor, um die Leistung zu optimieren, Kosten zu senken oder die Kundenzufriedenheit zu erhöhen.
- Support-Management: Geben Sie eine externe und objektive Perspektive, um strategische Entscheidungen zu leiten.
Erforderliche Fähigkeiten
- Solides Wissen über Hotelmanagement und Finanzanalyse.
- Beherrschung der Qualität, Sicherheit und Hotel regulatorische Standards.
- Fähigkeit zur Beobachtung, Analyse und Synthese.
- Kommunikationsfähigkeiten, um Ergebnisse zu präsentieren und das Management zu überzeugen.
- Ein Sinn für Lehre (Pädagogik) und Anleitung im Change Management.
- Gute Beherrschung von IT-Tools (Reporting, ERP, Hotelmanagement-Software).
- Fließende Fremdsprachenkenntnisse (insbesondere Englisch) sind eine Bereicherung für die Prüfung internationaler Einrichtungen.
Ausbildung zum Hotel Auditor
Ein Gradniveau von Bac + 3 bis Bac + 5 (Bachelor-zu Master-Äquivalent) ist in der Regel erforderlich:
- Bachelor in Hotelmanagement, Management, Audit oder Finanzen.
- MBA spezialisiert auf Hospitality Management oder in Audit und Management Control.
- Vorkenntnisse in der Hotellerie (Management, Revenue Management, Management Control, Qualität) werden sehr geschätzt.
Spezifische Zertifizierungen im Bereich Qualitätsaudit oder interne Kontrolle können den beruflichen Hintergrund ergänzen.
Gehalt eines Hotel Auditors
- Einstiegslevel: Zwischen 2.800 € und 3.500 € brutto pro Monat.
- Bestätigtes Profil (erlebt): Zwischen 3.500 € und 5.000 € brutto pro Monat.
- Senior oder Independent: Bis zu 6.000 € oder mehr, abhängig von der Größe und dem Ruf der geprüften Betriebe.
Karrierefortschritt
Nach einigen Jahren kann der Hotel Auditor zu Rollen wie:
- Qualitätsdirektor in einer Hotelkette.
- Management Controller, spezialisiert auf den Hotelbereich.
- Unabhängiger Berater in der Hotel- und Tourismusbranche.
- Hoteldirektor oder Abteilungsleiter (Accommodation, Catering, F&B) mit verstärkter Expertise in der Bedienungssteuerung.

Profils d'emploi
Commissaire aux comptes
L'hôtelier est un professionnel spécialisé dans l'évaluation des performances, de la conformité et de la rentabilité d'un hôtel ou d'un établissement touristique. Son rôle est d'analyser les pratiques de gestion, la qualité du service, la conformité réglementaire et la rentabilité afin de proposer des recommandations stratégiques. Véritable expert en contrôle et conseil, il aide les hôtels, les stations balnéaires et les chaînes hôtelières à optimiser leurs opérations et leur compétitivité.
Responsabilités
- Évaluer la gestion financière et opérationnelle : contrôler les budgets, les coûts, la facturation et les marges bénéficiaires.
- Analyser la conformité et la qualité du service : Vérifier le respect des normes d'hygiène, de sécurité et de qualité (ISO, labels hôteliers, normes de marque).
- Observer et vérifier les processus : Analyser l'organisation du travail dans divers ministères (hébergement, restauration, front office, ménage, F&B).
- Mesurer la satisfaction de la clientèle : Au moyen de sondages, d'audits mystères et d'examens en ligne.
- Formuler des recommandations stratégiques : Proposer des améliorations pour optimiser le rendement, réduire les coûts ou accroître la satisfaction des clients.
- Gestion du soutien : Fournir une perspective externe et objective pour guider les décisions stratégiques.
Compétences requises
- Bonne connaissance de la gestion hôtelière et de l'analyse financière.
- Maîtrise de la qualité, de la sécurité et des normes de réglementation hôtelière.
- Capacité d'observation, d'analyse et de synthèse.
- Compétences en communication pour présenter les résultats et convaincre la direction.
- Un sens de l'enseignement (pédagogie) et de l'orientation dans la gestion du changement.
- Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques (rapport, ERP, logiciel de gestion hôtelière).
- La maîtrise des langues étrangères (en particulier l'anglais) est un atout pour la vérification des établissements internationaux.
Éducation pour devenir auditeur d'hôtel
Un niveau de Bac+3 à Bac+5 (Bachelor à l'équivalent de Master) est généralement requis:
- Baccalauréat en gestion hôtelière, gestion, vérification ou finances.
- MBA spécialisé en gestion de l'accueil ou en audit et contrôle de gestion.
- L'expérience antérieure dans l'industrie hôtelière (gestion, gestion des revenus, contrôle de gestion, qualité) est très appréciée.
Des certifications spécifiques en matière d'audit de qualité ou de contrôle interne peuvent compléter les antécédents professionnels.
Salaire d'un auditeur hôtelier
- Niveau d'entrée: Entre 2 800 et 3 500 euros bruts par mois.
- Profil confirmé (Expérience): Entre 3 500 et 5 000 € brut par mois.
- Senior ou indépendant : jusqu'à 6 000 € ou plus, selon la taille et la réputation des établissements audités.
Évolution de carrière
Au bout de quelques années, l'auditeur hôtelier peut passer à des rôles tels que :
- Directeur qualité dans une chaîne hôtelière.
- Contrôleur de gestion spécialisé dans le secteur hôtelier.
- Consultant indépendant dans l'hôtellerie et le tourisme.
- Directeur d'hôtel ou chef de département (hébergement, restauration, F&B) avec une expertise renforcée dans la direction opérationnelle.
Réussites des diplômés de Vatel
En France et à l'international, les 50 000 anciens élèves du Vatel construisent chaque jour des carrières exemplaires, innovantes et passionnantes. Ils travaillent dans divers secteurs comme l'hospitalité de luxe, les restaurants gastronomiques, la gestion d'événements, le marketing hôtelier, la gestion de luxe, l'œnologie, les croisières, le tourisme international et l'industrie du vin et des spiritueux.

jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Head of Promotion and Distribution in the Agri-Food Industry
Do you want to combine commercial strategy with operational management in the agri-food sector? The role of Head of Promotion and Distribution offers you this opportunity. At the crossroads of marketing, logistics, and customer relations, this role plays a key part in developing sales and optimizing product presence in the market.
Main Responsibilities
The position combines commercial responsibilities , operational marketing , and distribution . The main tasks are:
- Develop the product promotion strategy: Implement commercial campaigns (in-store events, promotional actions, distributor partnerships).
- Ensure the management and coordination of distribution: Guarantee the availability of products at points of sale, optimize the supply chain, and manage stock rotation.
- Analyze commercial performance: Monitor indicators (sales, margins, promotional impact) and propose strategic adjustments.
- Supervise field teams: Oversee promoters, merchandisers, and area coordinators.
- Represent the brand to distributors: Negotiate agreements, enhance product visibility, and increase market share.
Required Skills and Qualities
- Commercial Skills: Mastery of negotiation techniques and customer relationship management.
- Operational Marketing: Ability to manage promotional campaigns and optimize product showcasing (merchandising).
- Logistics Knowledge: Understanding the challenges of distribution, the supply chain, and merchandising.
- Managerial Aptitudes: Ability to supervise and motivate a field team.
- Personal Qualities: Organizational skills, analytical mindset, dynamism, and a strong focus on results.
Education to Become a Head of Promotion and Distribution
The position is accessible after 3 to 5 years of post-secondary education (Bac+3 to Bac+5) in the following fields:
- Business / Marketing ( Bachelor Vatel , MBA Vatel Business School degree)
- Agri-food with a specialization in marketing & distribution
- Distribution and Retail Management
A specialized MBA in agri-food management or marketing/distribution strategy is an asset for progressing to management positions.
Salary
- Entry-level: €30,000 to €38,000 gross/year
- With experience (5-10 years): €40,000 to €55,000 gross/year
- Senior position or in a large company: up to €65,000 gross/year, with bonuses linked to commercial results.
Possible Career Progression
The Head of Promotion and Distribution can evolve into roles such as:
- Commercial Director (Sales Director)
- Category Manager
- Operational Marketing Manager
- Regional Sales Director
- Distribution Director

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. descriptionByLocale.it:
Profili di lavoro
Responsabile Promozione e Distribuzione nell'industria Agri-Food
Vuoi combinare la strategia commerciale con la gestione operativa nel settore agroalimentare? Il ruolo di Capo della Promozione e Distribuzione vi offre questa opportunità. All'incrocio tra marketing, logistica e relazioni con i clienti, questo ruolo svolge un ruolo chiave nello sviluppo delle vendite e nell'ottimizzazione della presenza dei prodotti sul mercato.
Principali responsabilità
La posizione combina responsabilità commerciali, marketing operativo e distribuzione. I compiti principali sono:
- Sviluppare la strategia di promozione del prodotto: implementare campagne commerciali (in-store eventi, azioni promozionali, partnership di distributori).
- Garantire la gestione e il coordinamento della distribuzione: garantire la disponibilità dei prodotti in punti vendita, ottimizzare la supply chain e gestire la rotazione delle scorte.
- Analizzare le prestazioni commerciali: Monitorare gli indicatori (vendita, margini, impatto promozionale) e proporre aggiustamenti strategici.
- Supervise team di campo: supervisionare promotori, commercianti e coordinatori di area.
- Rappresentare il marchio ai distributori: accordi di negoziazione, migliorare la visibilità dei prodotti e aumentare la quota di mercato.
Competenze e competenze richieste
- Competenze commerciali: padronanza delle tecniche di negoziazione e gestione delle relazioni con i clienti.
- Marketing Operativo: Capacità di gestire campagne promozionali e ottimizzare la presentazione del prodotto (merchandising).
- Conoscenza della logistica: comprensione delle sfide della distribuzione, della supply chain e della merchandising.
- Attitudini manageriali: Capacità di supervisionare e motivare un team di campo.
- QualitÃ personali: competenze organizzative, mentalità analitica, dinamismo e una forte attenzione ai risultati.
Istruzione per diventare un capo della promozione e della distribuzione
La posizione è accessibile dopo 3-5 anni di istruzione post-secondaria (Bac+3 a Bac+5) nei seguenti campi:
- Business / Marketing ( Bachelor Vatel , MBA Vatel Business School)
- Agri-food con una specializzazione in marketing e distribuzione
- Gestione distribuzione e vendita al dettaglio
Un MBA specializzato nella gestione agroalimentare o nella strategia di marketing/distribuzione è un vantaggio per il progresso nelle posizioni di gestione.
Salari

Job Profiles
Head of Promotion and Distribution in the Agri-Food Industry
Do you want to combine commercial strategy with operational management in the agri-food sector? The role of Head of Promotion and Distribution offers you this opportunity. At the crossroads of marketing, logistics, and customer relations, this role plays a key part in developing sales and optimizing product presence in the market.
Main Responsibilities
The position combines commercial responsibilities , operational marketing , and distribution . The main tasks are:
- Develop the product promotion strategy: Implement commercial campaigns (in-store events, promotional actions, distributor partnerships).
- Ensure the management and coordination of distribution: Guarantee the availability of products at points of sale, optimize the supply chain, and manage stock rotation.
- Analyze commercial performance: Monitor indicators (sales, margins, promotional impact) and propose strategic adjustments.
- Supervise field teams: Oversee promoters, merchandisers, and area coordinators.
- Represent the brand to distributors: Negotiate agreements, enhance product visibility, and increase market share.
Required Skills and Qualities
- Commercial Skills: Mastery of negotiation techniques and customer relationship management.
- Operational Marketing: Ability to manage promotional campaigns and optimize product showcasing (merchandising).
- Logistics Knowledge: Understanding the challenges of distribution, the supply chain, and merchandising.
- Managerial Aptitudes: Ability to supervise and motivate a field team.
- Personal Qualities: Organizational skills, analytical mindset, dynamism, and a strong focus on results.
Education to Become a Head of Promotion and Distribution
The position is accessible after 3 to 5 years of post-secondary education (Bac+3 to Bac+5) in the following fields:
- Business / Marketing ( Bachelor Vatel , MBA Vatel Business School degree)
- Agri-food with a specialization in marketing & distribution
- Distribution and Retail Management
A specialized MBA in agri-food management or marketing/distribution strategy is an asset for progressing to management positions.
Salary
- Entry-level: €30,000 to €38,000 gross/year
- With experience (5-10 years): €40,000 to €55,000 gross/year
- Senior position or in a large company: up to €65,000 gross/year, with bonuses linked to commercial results.
Possible Career Progression
The Head of Promotion and Distribution can evolve into roles such as:
- Commercial Director (Sales Director)
- Category Manager
- Operational Marketing Manager
- Regional Sales Director
- Distribution Director
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Leiter Promotion und Vertrieb in der Agrar-Lebensmittelindustrie
Möchten Sie die Geschäftsstrategie mit dem operativen Management im Agrar- und Lebensmittelsektor verbinden? Die Rolle des Head of Promotion and Distribution bietet Ihnen diese Möglichkeit. An der Kreuzung von Marketing, Logistik und Kundenbeziehungen spielt diese Rolle eine wichtige Rolle bei der Entwicklung des Vertriebs und der Optimierung der Produktpräsenz im Markt.
Hauptzuständigkeiten
Die Position kombiniert kommerzielle Verantwortlichkeiten, operatives Marketing und Vertrieb. Die Hauptaufgaben sind:
- Entwicklung der Produkt-Promotion-Strategie: Implementieren Sie kommerzielle Kampagnen (In-Store-Events, Werbeaktionen, Vertriebspartnerschaften).
- Gewährleistung der Verwaltung und Koordination des Vertriebs: Garantieren Sie die Verfügbarkeit von Produkten an Verkaufsstellen, optimieren Sie die Lieferkette und steuern Sie die Bestandsrotation.
- Analysieren Sie die kommerzielle Leistung: Überwachen Sie Indikatoren (Verkäufe, Margen, Werbewirkung) und schlagen Sie strategische Anpassungen vor.
- Beaufsichtigen Sie Feldteams: Beaufsichtigen Sie Promotoren, Merchandiser und Gebietskoordinatoren.
- Repräsentieren Sie die Marke für Distributoren: Verhandeln Sie Vereinbarungen, erhöhen Sie die Produkttransparenz und erhöhen Sie den Marktanteil.
Erforderliche Fähigkeiten und Qualitäten
- Kommerzielle Fähigkeiten: Beherrschung von Verhandlungstechniken und Customer Relationship Management.
- Operationelles Marketing: Fähigkeit, Werbekampagnen zu verwalten und Produktpräsentation (Merchandising) zu optimieren.
- Logistikwissen: Die Herausforderungen des Vertriebs, der Lieferkette und des Merchandising verstehen.
- Managementfähigkeiten: Fähigkeit, ein Feldteam zu beaufsichtigen und zu motivieren.
- Persönliche Qualitäten: Organisatorische Fähigkeiten, analytische Denkweise, Dynamik und ein starker Fokus auf Ergebnisse.
Bildung zum Head of Promotion and Distribution
Die Stelle ist nach 3 bis 5 Jahren postsekundärer Bildung (Bac+3 bis Bac+5) in den folgenden Bereichen zugänglich:
- Business / Marketing (Bachelor Vatel, MBA Vatel Business School)
- Agri-Food mit Spezialisierung auf Marketing & Vertrieb
- Distribution und Retail Management
Ein spezialisierter MBA in Agrar-Lebensmittel-Management oder Marketing / Distributionsstrategie ist ein Gewinn für den Fortschritt in Management-Positionen.
Gehalt
- Einstiegslevel: 30.000 € bis 38.000 € brutto/Jahr
- Mit Erfahrung (5-10 Jahre): 40.000 € bis 55.000 € brutto/Jahr
- Senior Position oder in einem großen Unternehmen: bis zu 65.000 € brutto / Jahr, mit Boni an kommerzielle Ergebnisse gebunden.
Mögliche berufliche Progression
Der Head of Promotion and Distribution kann sich zu Rollen entwickeln wie:
- Handelsdirektor (Vertriebsdirektor)
- Betriebsleiter
- Operations Marketing Manager
- Regional Sales Director
- Verteilungsleiter

Sie arbeiten in verschiedenen Bereichen wie Luxushotellerie, Gourmetrestaurants, Eventmanagement, Hotelmarketing, Luxusmanagement, Önologie, Kreuzfahrten, internationalem Tourismus und der Wein- und Spirituosenindustrie.

Profils d'emploi
Chef de la promotion et de la distribution dans l'industrie agroalimentaire
Voulez-vous combiner stratégie commerciale et gestion opérationnelle dans le secteur agroalimentaire? Le rôle de responsable de la promotion et de la distribution vous offre cette opportunité. Au carrefour du marketing, de la logistique et des relations client, ce rôle joue un rôle clé dans le développement des ventes et l'optimisation de la présence des produits sur le marché.
Principales responsabilités
Le poste combine les responsabilités commerciales , le marketing opérationnel et la distribution . Les principales tâches sont les suivantes:
- Élaborer la stratégie de promotion des produits : Mettre en oeuvre des campagnes commerciales (événements en magasin, actions promotionnelles, partenariats avec les distributeurs).
- Assurer la gestion et la coordination de la distribution : garantir la disponibilité des produits aux points de vente, optimiser la chaîne d'approvisionnement et gérer la rotation des stocks.
- Analyser les performances commerciales : Surveiller les indicateurs (ventes, marges, impact promotionnel) et proposer des ajustements stratégiques.
- Superviser les équipes de terrain : Superviser les promoteurs, les commerçants et les coordonnateurs régionaux.
- Représenter la marque aux distributeurs : Négocier des accords, améliorer la visibilité des produits et augmenter la part de marché.
Compétences et qualités requises
- Compétences commerciales : Maîtrise des techniques de négociation et gestion de la relation client.
- Marketing opérationnel : Capacité de gérer des campagnes promotionnelles et d'optimiser la présentation de produits (merchandising).
- Connaissance de la logistique : Comprendre les défis de la distribution, de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et du merchandising.
- Aptitudes de gestion : Capacité de superviser et de motiver une équipe de terrain.
- Qualités personnelles : Compétences organisationnelles, état d'esprit analytique, dynamisme et une forte concentration sur les résultats.
Éducation pour devenir chef de la promotion et de la distribution
Le poste est accessible après 3 à 5 années d'études postsecondaires (Bac+3 au Bac+5) dans les domaines suivants :
- Affaires / Marketing ( Baccalauréat Vatel , MBA Vatel école de commerce)
- Agroalimentaire avec spécialisation en marketing et distribution
- Distribution et gestion du commerce de détail
Un MBA spécialisé dans la gestion agroalimentaire ou la stratégie de commercialisation/distribution est un atout pour progresser vers des postes de gestion.
Salaire
- Niveau d'entrée: 30 000 à 38 000 euros brut/année
- Avec expérience (5-10 ans): 40 000 à 55 000 euros brut/an
- Fonction principale ou dans une grande entreprise: jusqu'à 65 000 € brut par an, avec des primes liées aux résultats commerciaux.
Évolution possible de la carrière
Le chef de la promotion et de la distribution peut évoluer vers des rôles tels que :
- Directeur commercial (Directeur des ventes)
- Gestionnaire de catégorie
- Directeur du marketing opérationnel
- Directeur régional des ventes
- Directeur de la distribution
Réussites des diplômés de Vatel
En France et à l'international, les 50 000 anciens élèves du Vatel construisent chaque jour des carrières exemplaires, innovantes et passionnantes. Ils travaillent dans divers secteurs comme l'hospitalité de luxe, les restaurants gastronomiques, la gestion d'événements, le marketing hôtelier, la gestion de luxe, l'œnologie, les croisières, le tourisme international et l'industrie du vin et des spiritueux.
